If the same refinement lemma must be re-sent after a user-context pop is irrelevant, but if liastar regenerates an identical node within the same user context it will be ignored -- the fresh skolems y/h per cell make lemmas syntactically distinct, so this should not bite in practice.

A variable v is MISSING from arithModel when: (a) v is not a subterm of any fact currently asserted to TheoryArith and not a shared term, hence not in termSet (theory_arith_private.cpp:4594) -- a fresh skolem appearing only in a lemma is present IFF at least one atom containing it has been assigned by the SAT solver and asserted to arith; for a lemma clause (~h OR base(y)-atoms), if h is true unit propagation forces the base(y) atoms so y IS in termSet/model; if h is false the atoms may stay unassigned under partial-assignment decision modes; (b) v was never preregistered/setup as an ArithVar (no atom over v ever reached the linear solver); (c) v is an auxiliary (slack) variable (theory_arith_private.cpp:4589); (d) v is an integer variable assigned a non-integral rational: it goes to arithModelIllTyped instead of arithModel (theory_arith_private.cpp:4600-4614) and at the time liastar runs sanityCheckIntegerModel has NOT yet repaired this (it runs at theory_arith.cpp:326, after :292); (e) v was eliminated by ppAssert/top-level substitution so it never occurs in asserted facts -- cannot happen for fresh skolems introduced after preprocessing.

Q1 DECISION-MODE NUANCE: whether all lemma atoms are assigned at full effort depends on options::decision::decisionMode. For the logics in which LiaStarExtension exists (TheoryArith::finishInit creates it only when logic is arith-enabled and !logic.isLinear(), theory_arith.cpp:94-100), SetDefaults::setDefaultDecisionMode (src/smt/set_defaults.cpp:1810-1877) yields DecisionMode::INTERNAL for e.g. QF_NIA (none of the JUSTIFICATION conditions at :1820-1845 match a quantifier-free pure-nonlinear-arith logic), so MiniSat produces a complete assignment at full effort and every preregistered arith atom (including lemma atoms over the skolems y and under guard h of either polarity) is asserted to TheoryArith -- so y lands in termSet and in arithModel. ANSWER Q3 (substitute+rewrite shortcut): the existing shortcut is liastar_extension.cpp:362-401 (guarded by options().arith.arithLiaStarModelValue, option defined in src/options/arith_options.toml:612): it flattens arithModel into parallel keys/values vectors (:368-375), builds check = vectorPredicate OR d_lastStarLia[literal] (:381-383), then Node value = check.substitute(keys.begin(), keys.end(), values.begin(), values.end()) followed by value = rewrite(value) (:385-387) and compares value == d_true (:391). For an arbitrary QF_LIA atom (comparisons over +, -, constant multiplication, integer constants) this is reliable IFF every free variable of the atom is a key in arithModel: substitution then yields a ground constant-only arith atom which the rewriter fully evaluates, and boolean connectives over constants fold, so the result is exactly d_true or d_false. If ANY free variable is missing from the map the result is a residual non-constant node (== neither d_true nor d_false); the current code treats that conservatively as 'not satisfied' and falls through to refinement (:402-410). Bound variables under closures are safe: Node::substitute is applied to vectorPredicate which is already the beta-reduced/instantiated predicate p[v] from LiaStarUtils::getVectorPredicate (liastar_extension.cpp:336-337), not the raw lambda.

caveats: Skolems under the guard h are only guaranteed to be in arithModel when at least one atom containing them was assigned and asserted to TheoryArith. Default decision mode for the liastar-enabled (nonlinear) quantifier-free arith logics is INTERNAL (complete SAT assignments), but with --decision=justification/stoponly or richer logics (strings, quantifiers, ALL), atoms in satisfied lemma clauses can remain unassigned and the skolems will be absent from the map. The enumeration code should fall back to TheoryArith::getCandidateModelValue or treat missing skolem values explicitly rather than assume presence.

Integer variables can transiently receive non-integral values: they are diverted to d_arithModelCacheIllTyped and are MISSING from the arithModel map at the time LiaStarExtension::checkFullEffort runs, because sanityCheckIntegerModel (which sends branch-and-bound lemmas) only runs afterwards (theory_arith.cpp:326 vs :292). Rare, but a robust evaluator must not assume an integer skolem key is present.

The substitute+rewrite shortcut yields d_true/d_false only when all free variables of the formula are covered by the map; a missing variable silently produces a non-constant residual, which the current code conservatively treats as 'model does not satisfy'. If the new enumeration logic needs a definite boolean (e.g. to decide whether to emit the next not(D_i(y)) lemma), it must check that the rewritten result is actually a constant.

arithModel keys are arbitrary non-auxiliary ArithVar nodes, not only variables/skolems (non-leaf terms like NONLINEAR_MULT abstractions appear); when building the substitution restrict to leaves if exact-term substitution into deeper terms is a concern (cf. finalizeModelCache's Theory::isLeafOf filter at theory_arith.cpp:559).

checkFullEffort for liastar is only reached when the linear solver is SAT and no lemma was sent earlier in postCheck; d_im.hasSent()/d_im.hasSentLemma() short-circuits inside checkFullEffort (liastar_extension.cpp:356-361) mean the model-based code may not run every round.
